Logistic Regression with Adam

Source: R/RcppExports.R
logistic_reg_adam.Rd

Solves logistic regression with the mini-batch Adam optimizer by expressing the negative log-likelihood as a separable objective function.

Usage

logistic_reg_adam(
  X,
  y,
  batch_size = 32L,
  max_epochs = 50L,
  step_size = 0.05,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

X

A matrix that is the Design Matrix for the regression problem. Include a column of ones for an intercept.

y

A vec of binary responses taking values 0 or 1.

batch_size

An integer giving the number of observations per mini-batch.

max_epochs

An integer giving the number of complete passes to make over the data.

step_size

A double giving the Adam step size. The default of 0.05 is deliberately larger than the 'ensmallen' Adam default of 0.001; see Details.

verbose

A logical indicating whether to report the loss at the end of each epoch through an ens::PrintLoss callback.

Value

The estimated \(\beta\) parameter values for the logistic regression.

Details

The objective and gradient match those of logistic_reg_lbfgs() with lambda = 0, but are evaluated one mini-batch at a time.

The optimizer's MaxIterations() counts data points visited, not batches and not epochs, so max_epochs is converted internally by multiplying by nrow(X).

As of 'ensmallen' 3.10 the SGD family divides the step size by the batch size, so a step size carried over from 'ensmallen' 2 will behave differently unless ENS_OLD_SEPARABLE_STEP_BEHAVIOR is defined. This is why step_size defaults to 0.05 rather than the 0.001 that ens::Adam itself uses: with a batch size of 32 the effective step is 0.001 / 32, roughly 3e-5, which leaves the optimizer far short of the optimum after 50 epochs.

Adam shuffles the data between epochs. That shuffle draws on Armadillo's random number generator, which 'RcppArmadillo' routes to R's own stream, so the result is reproducible under set.seed(). The flip side is that each call consumes random numbers from R's stream and therefore shifts any runif() or rnorm() draws that follow it. Without an explicit seed, successive calls start from different positions in the stream and so give slightly different answers.

Examples

# Number of Points
n = 5000

# Select beta parameters
beta = c(-1, 0.7, -0.5, 1.2)

# Number of Predictors (including intercept)
p = length(beta)

# Generate the design matrix with an intercept
X = cbind(1, matrix(rnorm(n * (p - 1)), ncol = p - 1))

# Generate binary responses
y = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 1 / (1 + exp(-X %*% beta)))

# Run optimization with Adam
theta_hat = logistic_reg_adam(X, y)

# Compare against the full-batch L-BFGS solution
cbind(actual = beta,
      adam = theta_hat,
      lbfgs = logistic_reg_lbfgs(X, y))
#>      actual                      
#> [1,]   -1.0 -0.9893675 -0.9897768
#> [2,]    0.7  0.7014957  0.6959250
#> [3,]   -0.5 -0.4562667 -0.4586689
#> [4,]    1.2  1.2423189  1.2408201
